Accessibility (A) and complementarity (C) on a road/trail network graph

Source: R/fn_network.R
network.Rd

A vector-first engine for the operational terms. Travel runs on the linestrings - roads and trails as a weighted igraph, each edge timed by its class speed - and only the last hop from the network to a patch centroid drops to an off-trail Tobler cost. This sidesteps the resolution trap of a friction raster (at 800 m a road is one fat cell) and, because the patches become graph nodes, the same network answers C (complementarity) for free.

Details

Model. Roads are the drive-to origins (reachable at zero walking cost); from there a crew walks trails (trail_speed) and finally cuts cross-country to the centroid at a slope-dependent Tobler speed. Accessibility of a patch is the least-cost path origin -> network -> hop, in hours.

Noding. OSM ways share vertex coordinates at junctions, so the graph is built by snapping segment endpoints to a snap-metre grid - correct for OSM topology. For arbitrary linework that crosses without shared vertices, pre-node it (e.g. sf::st_node) before calling.
